sections.h2: What is property tax like for a seller in Lincoln County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Lincoln County is the smallest of the four Georgia counties in the Census comparison, with Lincolnton as the seat where both tax offices operate. Owners here deal with a short list of offices, and most questions resolve in a single phone call.

The Census Bureau QuickFacts table gives 8,112 residents for mid-2025 on 210.38 square miles, or 36.6 per square mile in 2020. The 2010 census count was 7,996, the 2020 count 7,690, and the estimate has since climbed 5.5 percent from the 2020 base. Some 28.1 percent of residents are 65 or older, the highest share among the four counties, and 76.6 percent of housing units are owner-occupied at a median value of $165,900.

Money numbers are modest. Median household income is $56,907, median gross rent is $786 and owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,597 a month. Residents spend 31.2 minutes getting to work on average, the longest of the four, and only 64.5 percent of households have broadband. Builders pulled 55 permits in 2025. A seller should expect buyers who are older, settled and watching the annual bill closely.

sections.h2: Where are the Lincoln County tax commissioner and board of assessors?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner is at the courthouse on Humphrey Street in Lincolnton, and the assessors have a separate address one block down the same street.

Lincoln County property tax offices as printed on the county website
OfficeAddressPhoneHours
Tax Commissioner210 Humphrey Street, Lincolnton, GA 30817 (P.O. Box 946)706-359-5536Mon to Fri, 8:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.
Board of Tax Assessors182 Humphrey Street, Lincolnton, GA 30817 (P.O. Box 340)706-359-5502Mon to Fri, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

The county's assessor page describes the board's job as valuing all property in Lincoln County fairly and equitably, and it links to the qPublic record search. Its 2026 meeting schedule put the board's regular monthly meetings on the third Tuesday at 5:30 p.m. in the courthouse conference room. Changes are posted on the courthouse bulletin board and the assessors' front door.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Lincoln County property tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay in the commissioner's office, by mail or online with a credit card. Checks, cashier's checks and money orders must be payable to the Lincoln County Tax Commissioner.

The tax commissioner page lists what it takes:

  • Cash, check, cashier's check or money order at the counter.
  • American Express, Discover, Mastercard or Visa.
  • A 3 percent convenience fee on each credit card or online transaction.

The state's County Property Tax Facts page for Lincoln County says the official due date for ad valorem tax is December 20, though a county can move it to December 1 or November 15 or bill in installments. Each taxpayer gets 60 days from the postmark of the bill before interest starts, and delinquent tax may also pick up penalties. Read your bill for the date that applies, because the county pages do not print one.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Lincoln County assessment?
sections.html:
Send a written appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors, postmarked no later than 45 days after the mailing date on the assessment notice. The state facts page explains that the notice must tell you how to file, and the appeal goes to the board first.

Georgia law lets you pick one of three paths when you file:

  • The county Board of Equalization.
  • A hearing officer.
  • An arbitrator.

The Department of Revenue cannot override the board, the equalization board, a hearing officer, an arbitrator or Superior Court on a single appraisal. If the assessors have adopted a written policy of accepting email service, you may email the appeal. Ask the office at 706-359-5502 whether that policy is in place. Appeals can cover taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption, so the notice is the document to keep.

Returns of property for taxation are filed with the county tax office between January 1 and April 1. A taxpayer who skips a return is treated as having returned the same property at the same value as the year before.

sections.h2: What exemptions and refunds apply in Lincoln County?
sections.html:
Apply for the homestead exemption by April 1 of the first year you want it. Failure to apply is treated as a waiver. The Department of Revenue's page for Lincoln County lists no local homestead exemptions and says owners can apply for the statewide ones, so ask the commissioner whether that has changed.

Other provisions on the same state page:

  • Freeport: voters may exempt commercial and industrial inventory, and a late application can earn a partial exemption up to June 1.
  • Refunds: a written request for a refund of tax erroneously or illegally assessed must start within three years of payment, and a refund after a successful appeal is processed automatically once the final value is set.
  • Mobile homes: a location permit application goes to the commissioner within 30 days of permanent placement and again each year from January 1 to April 1.

Cities may also tax. The city clerk bills city tax unless the city and county have agreed to a single bill, so ask a Lincolnton owner's closing attorney whether a separate city bill exists.

sections.h2: What should I do about taxes when I sell a Lincoln County house?
sections.html:
Settle the year's tax at closing and confirm the bill is paid. The Department of Revenue says an owner on January 1 owes the whole year and cannot claim a refund for a part-year sale.

A few other state rules touch a sale. Anyone who holds a long-term note secured by real estate must record it in the county within 90 days, and the recording tax is $1.50 for each $500 or fractional part of the face amount of the note; most counties have the Clerk of Superior Court collect it. A vehicle bought after March 1, 2013 carries a one-time title ad valorem tax instead of the annual tax, which a seller moving with a vehicle should know.

Call the commissioner at 706-359-5536 for any balance. Because older residents make up a large share of the county, many owners hold a homestead or age-based exemption. Tell the buyer it does not carry over.

faqs.q: What are the Lincoln County tax commissioner's hours?
faqs.a: The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. at 210 Humphrey Street in Lincolnton.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to pay Lincoln County property tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes, a 3 percent convenience fee applies to credit card and online payments. Cash, checks and money orders carry no such fee on the county page.

faqs.q: When do I appeal a Lincoln County assessment?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of the date the notice was mailed. The appeal must be postmarked by that day and sent to the Board of Tax Assessors.

faqs.q: When are Lincoln County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 20 is the official state date unless the county changes it. Check the bill, because a county may use December 1, November 15 or installments.

faqs.q: Can I get a refund of Lincoln County tax if I overpaid?
faqs.a: Possibly. A written refund request must begin within three years of the payment date, and a refund after an appeal is processed once the final value is set.
